primary_provider.name: OpenAI Agents SDK for Python
why: Python-first path matches the current local control-plane codebase.
Fits the existing OpenAI/Codex key and model-routing plan.
Small agent primitives are easier to wrap behind Leon's approval, audit and assignment gates than a larger workflow platform.
Good first target for Personal Agent, Research Agent, code review, tool calls and multi-agent handoffs.
not_allowed_until: A provider adapter is implemented behind agent_assignment_proposals.
Tool scopes are capability-based, not raw secret/file access.
External write/tool execution requires a pending approval card and consumed approval id.
Trace/audit events redact prompt secrets and tool arguments.

secondary_options.name: LangGraph
secondary_options.use_when: Use if Leon needs explicit graph state, durable multi-step workflows, resumability and complex human-in-the-loop flow control beyond the local task queue.

secondary_options.name: Pydantic AI
secondary_options.use_when: Use if typed inputs/outputs, dependency injection and validation become more important than OpenAI-native handoffs for a specific component.

secondary_options.name: VoltAgent
secondary_options.use_when: Use only if the Leon interface/runtime moves strongly toward TypeScript and VoltAgent's observability/evals platform becomes worth the extra stack.

current_runtime.purpose: Exercise task packets, model routing, audit, review, and dashboard flows without external calls.

forbidden_without_explicit_gate: reading raw .env.local values inside agent context
GPU model downloads or heavy jobs
adapter_contract.secret_policy: Agents receive scoped capabilities and env-key presence metadata, never raw dashboard secret values.
adapter_contract.rate_limit_policy: Provider calls must return a retryable waiting state and integrate with leon-codex-resume-watch or a future queue worker.
